```{r analysis-data}
analysis_data <- raw_data %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    subject = factor(subject),
    sex = factor(sex)) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(subject, age) %>%
  dplyr::select(subject, age, sex, distance)
  
```


<!-- ===========================================================================
                       Analysis Overview 
=============================================================================-->
## **Analysis Overview** 

This analysis examines changes in craniofacial distance over time using the Orthodont dataset from the nlme R package. 
The dataset includes `r nrow(analysis_data)` measurements from `r dplyr::n_distinct(analysis_data$subject)` children (`r dplyr::n_distinct(analysis_data$subject[analysis_data$sex == "Male"])` boys and `r dplyr::n_distinct(analysis_data$subject[analysis_data$sex == "Female"])` girls), each assessed at ages 8, 10, 12, and 14 years.


We used linear mixed-effects models (LMMs) to account for repeated measurements within children and address two main research questions:

* Does craniofacial distance increase with age?

* Do boys and girls differ in their rates of change over time?

We compared random-intercept and random-intercept-plus-slope models to select an appropriate random-effects structure. We then evaluated the age × sex interaction to assess differences in growth rates between boys and girls.

Results include model comparisons, estimated annual changes with 95% confidence intervals, model-based predicted trajectories, and diagnostic assessments.


<!-- ===========================================================================
                       Overall Age effect on Distance
=============================================================================-->
## **Age Effect on Craniofacial Distance**

We used linear mixed-effects models to evaluate changes in craniofacial distance with age. Since each child was measured repeatedly, a random intercept was included to account for differences between children and within-child correlation.

To determine whether children also differed in their growth rates, we compared two models:

- **Random Intercept Only:** Allows each child to have a different baseline measurement but assumes the same growth rate.
- **Random Intercept + Random Slope:** Allows each child to have a different baseline measurement and growth rate.

The models were compared using a likelihood ratio test (LRT).


```{r age-models}
lmm_ri <- lme4::lmer(distance ~ age + (1 | subject), data = analysis_data, REML = FALSE)
lmm_ris <- lme4::lmer(distance ~ age + (age | subject), data = analysis_data, REML = FALSE)

age_models_comparison <- anova(lmm_ri, lmm_ris)
```

```{r age-model-comparison}
age_models_comparison %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  tibble::rownames_to_column("Model") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(Model = c("Random Intercept Only", "Random Intercept + Slope")) %>%
  dplyr::transmute(Model, AIC = sprintf("%.2f", AIC), BIC = sprintf("%.2f", BIC),
                   `LRT Chi-square` = round(Chisq, 2), df = Df,
                   `p-value` = Hmisc::format.pval(`Pr(>Chisq)`, digits = 3, eps = 0.001, na.form = "")) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(dplyr::everything(), ~ tidyr::replace_na(as.character(.x), "—"))) %>%
  kableExtra::kable(
    format = "html",
    escape = FALSE,
    digits = 3,
    row.names = FALSE,
    align = c("l", rep("r", 5)),
    caption = "Comparison of Random-Effects Structures"
    ) %>%
  kableExtra::kable_styling()
```

Adding a random slope did not significantly improve model fit (LRT: χ²(`r age_models_comparison$Df[2]`) = `r round(age_models_comparison$Chisq[2], 2)`, p = `r round(age_models_comparison[["Pr(>Chisq)"]][2], 3)`). Therefore, the simpler random-intercept model was selected.

The estimated annual change in craniofacial distance was `r round(lme4::fixef(lmm_ri)["age"], 3)` mm/year.

```{r age-effect}
age_effect <- emmeans::emtrends(lmm_ri, ~ 1, var = "age")

summary(age_effect, infer = c(TRUE, TRUE)) %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  dplyr::transmute(
    `Annual Change (mm/year)` = sprintf("%.3f", age.trend),
    `Lower 95% CI` = round(lower.CL, 3),
    `Upper 95% CI` = round(upper.CL, 3),
    `p-value` = Hmisc::format.pval(`p.value`, digits = 3, eps = 0.001, na.form = "")
  ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(Outcome = "Craniofacial Distance") %>%
  dplyr::relocate(Outcome, .before = 1) %>%
  kableExtra::kable(    format = "html",
    escape = FALSE,
    digits = 3,
    row.names = FALSE,
    align = c("l", rep("r", 4)),
    caption = "Estimated Annual Change in Craniofacial Distance")%>%
  kableExtra::kable_styling()
```

Model diagnostics were generally acceptable, with some deviations from normality in the distribution tails. All observations were retained.

<!-- ===========================================================================
                       Sex Effect on Distance 
=============================================================================-->
## **Sex Differences in Craniofacial Growth**

We evaluated whether boys and girls had different rates of change in craniofacial distance over time.

Two linear mixed-effects models with random intercepts were fitted:

- **Without Interaction:** Includes age and sex, assuming the same growth rate for boys and girls.
- **With Interaction:** Includes age, sex, and the age × sex interaction, allowing different growth rates for boys and girls.

We compared the models using a likelihood ratio test (LRT).

```{r sex-models}
lmm_sex_no_int <- lme4::lmer(distance ~ age + sex + (1 | subject), data = analysis_data, REML = FALSE)
lmm_sex <- lme4::lmer(distance ~ age * sex + (1 | subject), data = analysis_data, REML = FALSE)

sex_models_comparison <- anova(lmm_sex_no_int, lmm_sex)
```

```{r sex-model-comparison}
sex_models_comparison %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  tibble::rownames_to_column("Model") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(Model = c("Without Interaction", "With Interaction")) %>%
  dplyr::transmute(Model, AIC = round(AIC, 2), BIC = round(BIC, 2),
                   `LRT Chi-square` = round(Chisq, 2), df = Df,
                   `p-value` = Hmisc::format.pval(`Pr(>Chisq)`, digits = 3, eps = 0.001, na.form = "")) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(dplyr::everything(), ~ tidyr::replace_na(as.character(.x), "—"))) %>%
  kableExtra::kable(
    format = "html",
    escape = FALSE,
    digits = 3,
    row.names = FALSE,
    align = c("l", rep("r", 5)),
    caption = "Comparison of Models With and Without Age × Sex Interaction")%>%
  kableExtra::kable_styling()
```

Adding the age × sex interaction significantly improved model fit (LRT: χ²(`r sex_models_comparison$Df[2]`) = `r round(sex_models_comparison$Chisq[2], 2)`, p = `r round(sex_models_comparison[["Pr(>Chisq)"]][2], 3)`). Therefore, the interaction model was selected.

### Estimated Annual Growth Rates by Sex

We estimated the annual change in craniofacial distance for boys and girls using the selected model.

```{r growth-rates}
growth_rates <- emmeans::emtrends(lmm_sex, ~ sex, var = "age")
growth_results <- as.data.frame(summary(growth_rates, infer = c(TRUE, TRUE)))

growth_results %>%
  dplyr::transmute(
    Sex = sex,
    `Annual Change (mm/year)` = round(age.trend, 3),
    `Lower 95% CI` = round(lower.CL, 3),
    `Upper 95% CI` = round(upper.CL, 3),
    `p-value` = Hmisc::format.pval(`p.value`, digits = 3, eps = 0.001, na.form = "")
  ) %>%
  kableExtra::kable(
    format = "html",
    escape = FALSE,
    digits = 3,
    row.names = FALSE,
    align = c("l", rep("r", 4)),
    caption = "Estimated Annual Growth Rates by Sex")%>%
  kableExtra::kable_styling()
```

Craniofacial distance increased with age in both groups. The estimated annual increase was `r round(growth_results$age.trend[growth_results$sex == "Male"], 3)` mm/year for boys and `r round(growth_results$age.trend[growth_results$sex == "Female"], 3)` mm/year for girls. Boys showed a greater annual increase than girls.

### Model-Based Predicted Trajectories

We visualized the predicted mean craniofacial distance by age and sex using the selected interaction model. Shaded areas represent 95% confidence intervals.

Model-based predicted trajectories show that craniofacial distance increases with age in both boys and girls. Boys have higher predicted measurements and a steeper growth trajectory, consistent with the significant age × sex interaction. The difference between the predicted trajectories increases with age.

```{r predicted-trajectories, out.width="65%"}
pred_data <- emmeans::emmeans(lmm_sex, ~ sex | age,
                             at = list(age = seq(8, 14, 0.5))) %>%
  as.data.frame()

# ==============================================================================
if(FALSE){
ggplot2::ggplot(pred_data, ggplot2::aes(x = age, y = emmean, color = sex, fill = sex)) +
  ggplot2::geom_ribbon(ggplot2::aes(ymin = lower.CL, ymax = upper.CL), alpha = 0.15, color = NA) +
  ggplot2::geom_line(linewidth = 1.2) +
  ggplot2::scale_color_manual(values = sex_palette) +
  ggplot2::scale_fill_manual(values = sex_palette) +
  statwise::theme_statwise() +
  ggplot2::labs(title = "Model-Based Craniofacial Growth Trajectories by Sex",
                x = "Age (Years)", y = "Predicted Craniofacial Distance (mm)",
                color = "Sex", fill = "Sex")
}

# ==============================================================================
p_anim <- ggplot2::ggplot(pred_data, ggplot2::aes(x = age, y = emmean, color = sex, group = sex)) +
  ggplot2::geom_ribbon(ggplot2::aes(ymin = lower.CL, ymax = upper.CL, fill = sex), alpha = 0.15, color = NA) +
  ggplot2::geom_line(linewidth = 1.2) +
  ggplot2::geom_point(size = 2) +
  ggplot2::scale_color_manual(values = sex_palette) +
  ggplot2::scale_fill_manual(values = sex_palette) +
  ggplot2::coord_cartesian(xlim = c(8, 14), ylim = range(pred_data$lower.CL, pred_data$upper.CL)) +
  statwise::theme_statwise() +
  ggplot2::labs(title = "Craniofacial Growth by Sex | Age: {round(frame_along, 1)}",
                x = "Age (Years)", y = "Predicted Craniofacial Distance (mm)",
                color = "Sex", fill = "Sex") +
  gganimate::transition_reveal(age)

gganimate::animate(p_anim, nframes = 100, fps = 15, renderer = gganimate::gifski_renderer())
```

### Model Diagnostics

Model diagnostics indicated generally acceptable fit. Residuals showed no clear systematic pattern or substantial heteroscedasticity. Q-Q plots suggested approximate normality of residuals and random intercepts, with some deviations in the tails.

```{r final-model-diagnostics, fig.width=7, fig.height=5}
# Diagnostic data
diag_data <- tibble::tibble(
  fitted = fitted(lmm_sex),
  residual = resid(lmm_sex)
)

# 1. Residuals vs. Fitted
plot_res_fit <- ggplot2::ggplot(diag_data, ggplot2::aes(fitted, residual)) +
  ggplot2::geom_point(alpha = 0.6) +
  ggplot2::geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
  statwise::theme_statwise() +
  ggplot2::labs(title = "Residuals vs. Fitted",
                x = "Fitted Values", y = "Residuals")

# 2. Normal Q-Q Plot: Residuals
plot_qq_res <- ggplot2::ggplot(diag_data, ggplot2::aes(sample = residual)) +
  ggplot2::stat_qq() +
  ggplot2::stat_qq_line(color = "red3") +
  statwise::theme_statwise() +
  ggplot2::labs(title = "Normal Q-Q Plot: Residuals",
                x = "Theoretical Quantiles", y = "Sample Quantiles")

# 3. Normal Q-Q Plot: Random Intercepts
random_data <- tibble::tibble(
  intercept = lme4::ranef(lmm_sex)$subject[[1]]
)

plot_qq <- ggplot2::ggplot(random_data, ggplot2::aes(sample = intercept)) +
  ggplot2::stat_qq() +
  ggplot2::stat_qq_line(color = "red3") +
  statwise::theme_statwise() +
  ggplot2::labs(title = "Normal Q-Q Plot: Random Intercepts",
                x = "Theoretical Quantiles", y = "Sample Quantiles")


# ==============================================================================
statwise::radio_selector_1(
  options = c("Residuals vs. Fitted", "Normal Q-Q Plot: Residuals", "Normal Q-Q Plot: Random Intercepts"),
  content = list(plot_res_fit, plot_qq_res, plot_qq),
  id = "diagnostics",
  option_title = "",
  content_width = "65%",
  plot_height = 5
)
```


<!-- ===========================================================================
                       Summary
=============================================================================-->
## **Summary**

Craniofacial distance increased with age in both boys and girls. The random-intercept-only model was selected because adding a random slope `r if (age_models_comparison[["Pr(>Chisq)"]][2] < 0.05) "significantly improved" else "did not significantly improve"` model fit.

The age × sex interaction was `r if (sex_models_comparison[["Pr(>Chisq)"]][2] < 0.05) "statistically significant" else "not statistically significant"` (p = `r format.pval(sex_models_comparison[["Pr(>Chisq)"]][2], digits = 3)`), `r if (sex_models_comparison[["Pr(>Chisq)"]][2] < 0.05) "indicating that growth rates differed between boys and girls" else "providing insufficient evidence that growth rates differed between boys and girls"`. The estimated annual increase was `r sprintf("%.3f", summary(growth_rates)$age.trend[1])` mm/year (95% CI: `r sprintf("%.3f", summary(growth_rates)$lower.CL[1])`–`r sprintf("%.3f", summary(growth_rates)$upper.CL[1])`) for boys and `r sprintf("%.3f", summary(growth_rates)$age.trend[2])` mm/year (95% CI: `r sprintf("%.3f", summary(growth_rates)$lower.CL[2])`–`r sprintf("%.3f", summary(growth_rates)$upper.CL[2])`) for girls.

Model-based predicted trajectories showed `r if (summary(growth_rates)$age.trend[1] > summary(growth_rates)$age.trend[2]) "a steeper increase in craniofacial distance among boys" else if (summary(growth_rates)$age.trend[1] < summary(growth_rates)$age.trend[2]) "a steeper increase in craniofacial distance among girls" else "similar estimated growth rates in boys and girls"`. Model diagnostics indicated generally acceptable fit, with some deviations from normality in the distribution tails.

Overall, the analysis demonstrates how linear mixed-effects models can be used to evaluate longitudinal changes, account for repeated measurements, and compare growth trajectories between groups.
